analysis.title: GS US TMT .. quick hits ... (Peter Callahan, 3 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Flows and sentiment: October hurt risk appetite, but the NDX is up 60 bps on 11/3 led by Semis up about 2.5%. The desk saw a more balanced flow picture today versus few signs of defense over the prior few days. Earnings after the close include AMD and ANET.

The desk says the market is partly checking several boxes it has focused on: earnings, financing, oil and rates relief (for now), and positioning and valuation resets. The US mid-term election is that night. GS Economics expects the focus on DCs to fade somewhat after the election. The desk says it still feels hard to string together more than a few good days.

Top client inbounds: why Semis are so strong (CRDO, MPWR, TTMI, APH), Apple's outlook, strength in RBLX, RDDT and APP (up 5-7%), and weakness in DASH and online travel agencies. The desk is also getting heavy inbound on AMD and DDOG as potential disappointments ('bogeys').

Tonight's earnings list: ALAB, AMD, ANET, ANGI, BKNG, CPNG, DUOL, FLYW, FRSH, HURN, NVTS, OUST, PCOR, RVLV, SWKS, TOST, TREE, TRVG, XYZ. Most asked about: AMD 4Q guide expectations, ANET CY27 framing and BKNG 4Q guidance.

Software, especially 'inference economy' names: the bar is high. If growth is not accelerating in 3Q and into 4Q, the stocks are not going up. This is evident across NOW, FTNT, TWLO, PLTR, CHKP and DT. Focus next shifts to DDOG, NET, RBRK and OKTA.

2028 visibility: the market applies lower multiples to 2028 estimates in Semis and AI infrastructure because of limited perceived visibility. The desk lists several datapoints that could help the AI trade when risk appetite improves: AMZN guiding to 2027/2028 AWS growth, TSM saying AI demand is extremely robust with no sign of slowdown (it did not raise its long-term AI accelerator revenue CAGR), and Samsung saying memory supply tightness will last through 2028.

Further 2028 datapoints: SPCX said compute pricing is tracking slightly above the high end of the $30-$50 per watt range. AEIS said customers project demand strengthening through 2027 into 2028. STX said most of its nearline exabyte supply is allocated under long-term supply agreements through 2028.

Analog Semis (TXN, NXPI, MPWR, ON): price action has been choppy, but the desk sees more of a 'glass half full' tone in results and price action than in other parts of the Semis tape. Yesterday's ISM Manufacturing print was better than expected. IFX, STM and MCHP report in coming days.

Internet: early signs of GenAI becoming a tailwind to e-commerce growth (personalization, cataloging, listings), cited by ETSY, EBAY and CVNA. Advertising results are choppy (PINS cited EU headwinds). RDDT flagged user-side effects from search referral traffic changes as AI workflows shift.

IT services show renewed pressure: IT fell 13% on 11/3 after ex-US federal contract value grew only 2.8% y/y, and Gartner no longer expects to reach its prior 4% year-end target (per GIR). CTSH guided lighter for 4Q on weaker discretionary spending in Healthcare and Consumer, and INFY cut guidance on sluggish demand and a shift in client spend priorities.

Consumer: US spending remains strong. Visa and Mastercard both showed underlying beat-the-estimate results, particularly quarter to date, with October payment volume tracking better than expected despite step-downs from a strong September. Both described the consumer backdrop as healthy and resilient with no notable weakness across consumer bands.

Chart of the day: Info Tech and Communication Services together accounted for more than 60% of S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3, yet sit at the bottom of the table for T+1 returns. The market has been very discerning on tech earnings.
